reference_sql:
WITH ranked AS (  -- one row per lead
  SELECT email, source,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY email ORDER BY created_at, lead_id) AS rn
  FROM leads
)
SELECT source, COUNT(*) AS contacts
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1
GROUP BY source
alternatives:
WITH firsts AS (  -- one row per email
  SELECT email, MIN(created_at) AS created_at
  FROM leads
  GROUP BY email
),
first_ids AS (  -- one row per email
  SELECT l.email, MIN(l.lead_id) AS lead_id
  FROM leads l
  JOIN firsts f ON f.email = l.email AND f.created_at = l.created_at
  GROUP BY l.email
)
SELECT l.source, COUNT(*) AS contacts
FROM first_ids fi
JOIN leads l ON l.lead_id = fi.lead_id
GROUP BY l.source

SELECT t.source, COUNT(*) AS contacts
FROM (
  -- one row per lead, numbered within its email from the earliest
  SELECT email, source,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY email ORDER BY created_at, lead_id) AS rn
  FROM leads
) AS t
WHERE t.rn = 1
GROUP BY t.source

),

  SELECT l.email, MIN(l.lead_id) AS lead_id
  FROM leads l
  JOIN firsts f ON f.email = l.email AND f.created_at = l.created_at

)
SELECT l.source, COUNT(*) AS contacts
FROM first_ids fi
JOIN leads l ON l.lead_id = fi.lead_id
GROUP BY l.source
other_way.tradeoff: The earliest time per email, then the lowest lead_id at it, needs no window but takes two grouping steps and a join back.

solver.query:

SELECT source, COUNT(*) AS contacts FROM r WHERE rn = 1 GROUP BY source
